get.description:
Answers `200` with `ok` for as long as the process runs, whatever its
dependencies say: an orchestrator restarts a process that stops
answering here. Served on the internal listener only, and asks nothing
of anyone.

Asks the database, the message bus and the cache, and answers `200`
when every one answers and `503` when one does not or the check runs
out of time. Neither answer has a body: which dependency failed, and
why, goes to the operator's logs, never to the caller. Served on the
internal listener only, with no credentials asked of the orchestrator's
probe: on the public one, anyone could make the platform ask all three
as often as they liked, and learn which of them is down.

post.summary: Answer the gateway's question about an approval (gateway only)
post.description:
The gateway never writes approvals. When an agent's action needs a
person's approval it asks here, sealed, either to hold the action (find
the request a person decides for exactly that action, or open one,
unless the delegation already has too many open) or to spend the
approval a person gave, once. Opening a request records
`agents.approval_requested`.

Served only on the internal listener, which no ingress routes to. The
question must carry the gateway's seal, under the key of this channel
alone, a recent timestamp and a nonce not seen before. Every answer is
`200` with a typed result; anything that fails, an unsealed, stale or
repeated question included, is answered `refused`, and the gateway
refuses the action.

The answer goes back sealed in `x-ianua-seal`, under the same channel's
key and bound to the question's nonce; a question that did not open gets
its refusal unsealed. The gateway takes no answer without a seal for its
own question, so nobody else on the internal network can admit an
agent's action, nor replay an earlier answer.

requestBody.description: The sealed question, exactly as the gateway sealed it

200.description: The answer, or a refusal, for the gateway to act on, sealed for the question it answers

x-ianua-seal.description: The API's seal over the answer, bound to the question's nonce; absent when the question did not open

post.description:
Serves app-host password, factor, mail and provider sign-ins, passkeys,
password resets, signup, address verification, sign-out, service tokens,
sign-in pages and cross-host session handoffs through the gateway.
Runs only on the internal listener, outside ingress routing. Unsealed,
stale or replayed requests receive an empty `401`; other requests receive
`200` with a typed outcome, including refusals. Client address and user
agent come from the sealed body. `Accepted` replies use the dashboard's
timing floor to conceal whether an address has an account.
Replies carry `x-ianua-seal`, signed with the channel key and bound to
the request nonce; the gateway refuses unsigned or substituted answers.

requestBody.description: The sealed request, exactly as the gateway sealed it

200.description: The outcome, or the refusal, for the gateway to act on, sealed for the request it answers

x-ianua-seal.description: The API's seal over the answer, bound to the request's nonce

401.description: Unsealed, stale or seen before; the body is empty

get.description:
The process's own metrics in the Prometheus text format: how it runs,
never what any tenant holds. Served on the internal listener only, where
the scraper calls; the public listener has no such route.

200.description: The process's metrics, in the Prometheus text format

500.description: The metrics could not be written out

ChallengeCode.description: A kind of challenge a sign-in may be asked to solve.

ErrorBody.description: Structured JSON error body returned to API consumers.

oneOf.description:
The challenge to solve before signing in again, on
`challenge_required` when one can be set. Absent when none can: only
a trusted device or single sign-on gets in until the pressure eases.

details.description: Internal error details (only present in development mode).

key.description:
The message key of `message`, when it has one, such as
`routing-cannot-move-a-route-from-to`: a client may show the
message in its own words from the key and `params`.

message.description:
Human-readable message, in the first language of `Accept-Language`
the platform words it in, else in English.

params.description: The values `message` was filled with, by name.

ErrorCode.description: Fixed set of machine-readable error codes.
